text.p: The Polish subsidiary of German Bayerische Hypotheken-und Wechselbank AG, HYPO-BANK Poland SA, plans to set up a network of at least 15 to 20 branches, the head of the Polish unit's supervisory board said on Thursday.

HYPO-BANK opened its first Polish branch in Poznan last October, after launching a Warsaw subsidiary early in 1996, and planned to open three more branches in Wroclaw, Szczecin and Lodz before the end of this year, Hans Friedl said.
"We can assume a minimum of 15 to 20 Polish branches in the longer term," Friedl told a news conference.

In the first year of operations, HYPO-BANK Poland increased its capital to 89.5 million zlotys and showed a net loss of 6.7 million due to high start-up costs, the Polish unit's president Jorg Dorka, also present, said.
Friendl said HYPO-BANK Poland, which in future wants to focus on mortgage financing, may brake even in 1997.
The German bank also has subsidiary banks in Prague, Budapest and Bratislava. It also plans to transform a Moscow representative office into a bank in 1997.
